## What

Resolve https://github.com/nickderobertis/oneharness/issues/1290, accepted at severity
`high`: Claude Code's login refusal is classified as a rate limit.

`crates/oneharness-core/src/domain/signals.rs:902-957` scans the generic failure vocabulary
with rate-limit phrases ahead of auth, and the auth list omits both `not logged in` and
`/login`. So a zero-token failed result whose text says
`Not logged in · Please run /login` is recorded with `failure_kind: "rate_limit"` and a
fall-through reason of `rate-limit`, because unrelated text in the same failed run decides
the classification. That is what oneharness 0.12.1 recorded against an empty Claude
configuration directory on a real host.

Add the Claude login refusal as an **adapter-specific auth precondition, checked ahead of
the generic vocabulary**. The structure for that already exists:
`classify_harness_failure` checks the harness-aware quota signal, then the precondition
refusals, then the unknown-session rejection, and only then falls through to the generic
`classify_failure` — and its own doc comment says why that order is load-bearing. Scope the
phrase to the Claude dialect rather than making it dialect-agnostic, so another harness's
unrelated text cannot be read as a login refusal, and keep the existing bound that a
candidate with work evidence never falls through: an agent that merely wrote the sentence
mid-run must not hand its task on.

Cover a failed stream-json result that carries the refusal **and** unrelated warning text
in the same output, since that mixture is what the misclassification came from.

## Why

The user accepted this at `high` severity after hitting it on their own host. An
unauthenticated Claude identity reported as rate-limited sends an operator to the wrong
remedy entirely: they wait out a limit that does not exist, or go looking for quota, when
the fix is to authenticate the named configuration directory. The fall-through reason is
wrong for the same reason, so the chain's own record of why it moved on is misleading. The
workaround is reading raw result text by hand, which is what a failure classifier exists to
save an operator from doing.

## Acceptance criteria

- A failed Claude-dialect result whose text carries the login refusal is classified as an
  authentication failure, and its fall-through reason says auth rather than rate limit.
- That classification holds when the same failed output also carries unrelated warning text
  and rate-limit vocabulary, so the refusal decides the reading rather than the neighbouring
  text.
- The phrase is recognized for the Claude dialect and not for another harness's output, so
  an unrelated CLI's text carrying similar words is classified as it was before.
- A candidate with work evidence still does not fall through on this signal, so an agent
  that wrote the sentence mid-run cannot hand its task on.
- Every behaviour above is proven by tests driving the real classifier over real captured
  result text rather than by inspection, and no test substitutes a double for the layer
  under test.
- The commit body carries a `Closes` line naming
  https://github.com/nickderobertis/oneharness/issues/1290.
- The crate tests that cover the classifier are green over the finished tree, and so is the
  judged lint over this change's diff.
- Every claim this dispatch makes about the finished work is true of the tree as it finally
  stands.

## Additional info

Iterate with this repository's diff-scoped judged lint and the crate tests over the
classifier rather than its whole gate, which builds and smokes artifacts this change cannot
affect. The repository's own required checks run downstream on the change this branch
becomes; nothing here asks you to have run them first.

This repository publishes the reusable engine as its own crate target, separately from the
CLI, and a consumer in this plan waits on that crate: a node of `onepipeline` relinks
`oneharness-core` to the release carrying this fix, and this host's engine pin then adopts
it. Two consequences for your commit. Its type decides what release carries it, so a type
that cuts no release would leave the classifier unreleased and two nodes waiting
indefinitely. And the consumer's own resolution has to stay compatible with what
`oneagentgraph` and `onejudge` require of `oneharness-core`, so keep the change within the
engine's current minor version; if you find you cannot, raise it over
`$ORCHESTRATOR_ASK_MANAGER` rather than deciding the version story yourself.

Board items on the follow-ups board are not yours to move — its credential is masked from
every dispatch. The `Closes` line is the whole of what this node does about the issue.

## Additional info

### Operational notes for this host

**Run only the checks that exercise what you changed.** The tests that cover the code
you touched, the lint that reads your diff — and nothing wider. The repository's own
automation runs the full bar downstream on the change this work becomes: a `pre-push`
hook where that repository publishes locally, the host's required checks where it
publishes remotely. Neither is waiting for you to have run it first, so running it here
spends twenty to forty minutes of this dispatch learning what the merge path reports
anyway. That is measured rather than estimated: one node in this workstream spent about
84 minutes on three rounds of everything its repository could run, to reach lint findings
a diff-scoped run reports in two.

**Pick those checks from your change, and take the narrowest scope each one supports.**
One test module over the whole suite; the lint over your diff over the lint over the
tree. A repository's own fast deterministic tier is a fine choice when it is what
exercises your change — its `just --list` says which recipe that is — and a poor one when
you reached for it because it was the widest thing available. When a check you ran
reports something, fix that and run **that check** again; nothing here asks you to re-run
its neighbours to confirm, and a wider tier cannot re-check a finding it never made.

**A dispatch that changed nothing tracked owes none of them.** When your deliverable is a
document, a report, or an answer, there is no changed code for those checks to exercise
and you are complete without them — decide that from what the repository shows, never
because running them is slow or inconvenient. `git status` reporting nothing to commit is
then a correct and complete outcome, not a problem to solve by writing a file nobody
asked for.

**Never signal a process you did not identify by PID, and a PID you got from a pattern is
still a pattern kill.** Several managers share this host, and their dispatches, drivers,
publications and test servers run under the same few binary names — `just`, `node`,
`python`, `onepipeline-api` — so a kill by name knows nothing about *whose* work it
matched. The distinction is the tool rather than the pattern: `pgrep` and `ps` **read**,
and either spelling of them is fine, `pgrep -x` included; `pkill` **signals**, and it is
never the answer here, in any spelling. `-x` is the trap, because it reads as the careful
one — `pkill -f 'just gate'` at least needs a narrowing pattern, while `pkill -x just`
takes every `just` on the machine. Reading the table first and piping the pids into `kill`
is no way around it: that is the same pattern kill with more steps.

Two workers reached that place from different directions on 2026-08-24, while another
manager's dispatch had been live over an hour. One ran `pkill -TERM -x just`. The other
ran `ps -eo pid,args | grep 'onepipeline-api serve' | awk '{print $1}' | while read pid;
do kill "$pid"; done` — which obeys the letter of every paragraph below and does the same
damage, because `just dag-ui` and the e2e suites both spawn that server and a pytest run's
were alive at that moment.

**The one process you may signal is one you started yourself, so capture its PID as you
start it:**

    cmd & MYPID=$!
    kill "$MYPID"

Anything you did not start belongs to somebody. Read what it is, report what you found,
and leave it running.

**A wait written against a full command line never ends, because one of those command
lines is yours.** That is a different defect from the one above — it wedges your own
dispatch rather than somebody else's — and it is why `pgrep -f` cannot be waited on.
`pgrep -f` matches its pattern against every process's whole argv and excludes exactly one
process — itself — never the shell that invoked it. So any pattern naming the thing you are
waiting for is, by construction, a substring of the command line of the shell doing the
waiting: `until ! pgrep -f "just gate"` matches its own loop and never exits, and so does
the same loop written against `llmlint-judge.sh`, `scripts/fetch-corpus.sh`, or
`publish-branch`. That is a defect in the polling mechanism rather than a fact about gates,
so it applies to every wait you write.

That has wedged four workers here, and then two more workers and the manager itself in one
night: seven instances of one defect. A crozier corpus audit waited in `until ! pgrep -f
'scripts/fetch-corpus.sh'` with no fetch running at all — the only two matches were its own
polling shell and the manager's diagnostic shell — and waited until it was interrupted. A
`check-plan-bar-conflict` dispatch waited on `! pgrep -f "llmlint-judge.sh"`, whose negation
could never become true, and was cancelled and killed; its replacement then reached for
`pkill -f` against three patterns, which is not a wait at all but the same self-match with a
signal attached, and is refused above. And the manager, an hour after instructing a worker
about this, guarded a launch with `pgrep -f "publish-branch" && echo ABORT || launch`, whose
pattern was a literal substring of the launching shell's own command line: it aborted
unconditionally and then reported a publish as RUNNING that did not exist. That last one is
the evidence that matters most — a rule its own author reproduces an hour after issuing it
is a rule whose wording is the problem rather than its reader.

**Wait with a sentinel file.** Background the whole command you are waiting on — one
command, so that what you waited on is what you meant to run — and poll for a file only
that invocation can write:

    ( just test > /tmp/check.$$.log 2>&1; echo $? > /tmp/check.$$.exit ) &
    until [ -f /tmp/check.$$.exit ]; do sleep 20; done

**A process must finish inside the turn that started it.** Backgrounding is how you wait
on a slow command *within* one turn, which is why the launch and the wait sit together in
that example — both halves belong to the same turn. What does not survive is a background
process left running when the turn ends: nothing carries it across, and the launch gives
you no sign of that, because it succeeded and the turn then ended normally. The loss
shows up a turn later as a sentinel that never appeared and a recipe terminated by
signal, with the whole run to pay for again. It bites hardest where it is most tempting,
because a worker reaches for backgrounding exactly when a command is slow enough to
threaten the turn — here the judged lint tier and a whole test tier, which are the two
runs a node most needs to have made. So run a slow check in the foreground, or background
it and wait out its sentinel before your turn ends; never end a turn intending to read a
result on the next one.

**To ask whether a process is running at all, match the executable, not the command line.**
`pgrep -x onepipeline` matches process *names* exactly — the binary, not its arguments — so
the shell doing the asking, whose own name is `bash`, cannot match it however the pattern
is spelled. Where the binary name is not distinctive enough to identify what you mean
(`just`, `node` and `python` run everything), read the process table instead and drop the
one self-match that form has:

    ps -eo pid,args | grep -v grep | grep 'lint-llm-diff'

Both of those are **reads**, which is what makes `-x` safe here and forbidden the moment
the tool signals. The replacement for the worker wedged above reached for `pkill -f "just
gate"`, `pkill -f "just check"` and `pkill -f "nx run"` while another manager's run was
live. Read to learn what is running, report what you found, and signal nothing you did not
start.

**One sentinel and one log per invocation, and look before you launch one.** That pair is a
shape rather than two literal paths. Several dispatches run on this host at once and they
share `/tmp`, so a second worker writing `/tmp/check.log` writes into the first one's — and
`until [ -f /tmp/check.exit ]` returns immediately on somebody else's exit file, reporting
their result as yours. Name both after the invocation (`/tmp/check.$$.log`, or the node
id), and, before starting it, check whether its sentinel path is already in use by another
invocation; if so, choose a different invocation-specific pair. This path-ownership check
does not prohibit concurrent checks or judged tiers. Three workers collided on shared names
today and not one of the three failures read as what it was: two
deterministic-tier runs deadlocked against the same cargo target-directory lock, so both
logs sat unchanged and neither progressed — about fifteen minutes lost and three
interruptions to a live turn; two whole-e2e runs wrote to one log, and stopping the
duplicate left four `SIGTERM` entries in it that read exactly like real test failures; two
judged-tier runs raced and wasted a roll, which was harmless only by luck. Read a log that
has stopped growing as two commands blocking each other before you read it as one command
working.

<!-- llmlint: ignore[contracts_have_one_source_or_a_drift_gate] The source of this contract is the engine that exports the variable, and it lands in the same run as this paragraph: there is no released copy to reconcile against yet, and this task is explicitly told not to go looking for one in an installed engine. `tests/test_dispatch_appendix.py` holds these four properties and no more, so the day the engine side is adopted the drift gate has an exact set to reconcile. -->
**Write the files this dispatch needs under `ONEPIPELINE_NODE_SCRATCH_DIR`, rather than
under a `/tmp` path you invented.** It is an absolute path to a directory that exists and
is writable when the dispatch starts, is unique to this dispatch, and is not removed while
it runs.

**Root-owned files after a container run.** The pre-push visual guard captures in Docker
as root and can leave `.nx/` and `dist/` unwritable, failing the *next* check with `NX
Permission denied (os error 13)`. There is no passwordless sudo; repair from inside a
container:

    docker run --rm -v "$PWD":/w -w /w mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.61.1-noble \
      chown -R "$(id -u):$(id -g)" /w

**If a test fails in a way that makes no sense, check the host before the test.** On
2026-08-19 two publication attempts against the same already-green branch failed on two
unrelated tests — a 5-second timeout, then a browser remote that never came up — and both
were written up as flakes. The host was at 197G/197G, and the next attempt said so
outright with `No space left on device`. A full disk does not announce itself to a test
runner; it announces itself as an unrelated test failing. One command rules it out:

    df -h /home .

**The judged lint tier is nondeterministic**, wherever a repository runs one. It has
already returned opposite verdicts on an identical diff in this workstream. Clear the
findings it names, then stop — do not re-run hunting a clean sheet. If a rule looks wrong
or misapplied, say so with evidence rather than editing it.

**One suppression policy, and this is the whole of it.** A site-scoped `ignore` directive
is permitted where the rule is genuinely misapplied at that site **and** the directive
carries a substantive reason saying why. What is forbidden is silencing a finding you
have not answered so that a count moves. What you owe an account of is **every
suppression your own diff writes — added, moved or rewritten — and every one already
standing over a line that diff changes** — each with its site and its reason, in your
completion report, so the manager reads what you left rather than discovering it. Both
halves are decided from the diff alone: a directive line inside it, or a changed line
inside the region a directive covers. A file-scoped directive is outside both unless your
diff writes the directive itself — its region is every line of the file, so counting it
would make this file's own header a debt of every change that edits a word of it.
Suppressions elsewhere in the tree are not yours to inventory: this repository carries several hundred standing directives, and
a list of them would be longer than the report is read under while saying nothing about
the change under review.

That scope is stated because the sentence it replaces read two ways at once: its first
clause reached every directive anywhere in the repository, while its second — *so the
manager reads what you left* — was about this dispatch's own work, in the same breath. A
node was failed on the wider reading for not accounting for suppressions it had never
touched, on a tree whose every target had just run from cold and come back green; it cost
a third dispatch of a run's final node. The reading above is the one the purpose clause
and the scale both support, and it is written so that a worker complying with it and a
judge reading it adversarially land in the same place. It says which lines rather than which sites for the same
reason: *site* was itself readable two ways, and the first worker to apply the sentence
could not decide whether the file-scoped directives at the head of `AGENTS.md` were
owed by a change that edits one of its paragraphs. Apply that same test to whatever
replaces it: read it as a worker trying to comply and as a judge looking for a way to
refuse, and if the two can land in different places it is not one source yet.

`AGENTS.md` states no suppression policy of its own and points here, because this file is
what your judge reads beside your task: while that document said it twice, one
dispatch added four site-scoped ignores each carrying a substantive reason and was failed
for *"the task's categorical instruction never to suppress a rule"* — work that was
correct under one of this repository's own readings and refused under the other.

**`--no-verify` is not an acceptable response to a slow or inconvenient hook.** The hooks
are this repository's enforcement point — there is no CI — so bypassing one commits work
that nothing has checked, and nothing you run afterwards catches it: a check runs over
the finished tree, by which point a bypassed commit is simply history. Two workers
today reached for `git commit --no-verify`, both on a commit they had judged mechanical,
and one of the two was a *merge* commit — a conflict resolution, which is the single most
likely commit in a dispatch to be wrong. No check caught either one; the monitor caught
both. If a hook is slow, wait for it. If it refuses, it is telling you something about the
commit in front of you, and the answer is to fix the commit.

**Commit a coherent working piece the moment it works.** A dirty worktree does not
survive this dispatch: what is uncommitted when your last turn ends is what nothing
recovers — not a retry, not a recovery verb, not a manager reading the branch. So each
piece is its own commit as you finish it, rather than one commit held back to the end.
*The moment it works* is the moment you have seen it work: the checks that piece needs
are run before it is committed rather than after, so that each commit is one you have
evidence for.

**Ask rather than stop.** When you cannot proceed without a decision that is not yours —
a frozen contract you would have to amend, a goal that reads two ways, a constraint you
would have to relax — put the question to your manager over `$ORCHESTRATOR_ASK_MANAGER`,
which every dispatch carries, and go on working on whatever does not depend on the answer.
Ending your turns with the work undone and the question unasked is the one response
nothing can recover: a worker that reasoned about a frozen contract correctly, declined to
amend it unilaterally, named two options for its owner, and then stopped for three turns
lost about fifteen minutes of correct work and settled reporting `ahead of main: 0
commit(s)`.

**Draft a follow-up that can wait; never draft one that cannot.** Work you notice that
is outside your subtask — a bug beside the code you touched, a missing test or script, a
stale document, an improvement to this harness or to the context agents are given — is a
follow-up, and doing it is not yours. Record each one the moment you notice it by piping
its body into `"$ORCHESTRATOR_FOLLOW_UP_DRAFT"`, whose `--help` names the flags and the four
headings that body carries; the command stamps where it came from. Do not collect them into
a list at the end of your last message instead, because nothing reads that list. A draft is
unverified — a follow-up agent checks every one after the run — and it is not your
completion report, which still says what you did. Drafting is only for what can wait:
anything blocking, whether a decision fork, a constraint you cannot meet, or something your
manager should act on now, goes over `$ORCHESTRATOR_ASK_MANAGER` immediately, as the
paragraph above says, and is never drafted in its place.

**A GitHub rate-limit refusal that `gh api rate_limit` disagrees with is the secondary
limiter.** The primary limit is the one that endpoint reports and the one a wait answers.
The secondary limiter is reported by nothing, polled by nothing, and not waited out by
polling — every further attempt extends it. So when a `gh` call is refused for a rate
limit while `gh api rate_limit` still shows budget, stop making that call: deliver the
result another way, name in your report what was refused and what you tried, and leave the
retry to a person.

**Publication goes through the harness.** The session branch reaches its remote only
through `onevcs publish "$ONEVCS_SESSION"`, and its change request is lifted and landed
by the lifecycle after you settle. No `git push` of the session branch, no `gh pr create`
for it, no `gh pr ready`, no `gh pr merge`. Finish the branch, commit everything, leave
the tree clean, and report. Landing it is explicitly **not** yours to perform and **not**
part of your acceptance criteria. Two things are yours, and each only when this task's
own `## Additional info` — its own words above these notes — says so:

- **Only when the task's `## Additional info` says the change request may be published
  early**: `onevcs publish "$ONEVCS_SESSION" --draft [--title T] [--body-file PATH]` opens
  the session's change request as a draft, and a later `publish --draft` pushes new
  commits onto that same change request and never opens a second. Commit everything
  first — a dirty tree is committed for you, under a provenance you did not choose.
  `onevcs change describe "$ONEVCS_SESSION" --body-file PATH` replaces its description
  and `onevcs change show "$ONEVCS_SESSION"` reads it back. The description you leave is
  what the drafter finishes from, so start it with what only you know — the evidence and
  where it is. Never mark the draft ready; the lifecycle does, after the description is
  finished. `ONEVCS_SESSION` is in every lifecycle dispatch's environment.
- **Only when the task's `## Additional info` authorizes a throwaway demonstration change
  request**: after the draft is open, cut a branch from the session branch, commit the
  demonstration on it, push it with `git push -u origin <branch>`, open it with
  `gh pr create --draft --base <session branch> --head <branch> --title "DO NOT MERGE: …"`,
  capture the evidence — `gh pr view <n> --comments`, `gh pr checks <n>`, and `gh api`
  **reads** of that change request's own comments, checks and reviews, never a write to
  anything — then close it with `gh pr close <n> --delete-branch`, return to the session
  branch, and delete the local branch — a local branch left behind makes the session's
  close refuse. Its base is always the session branch, never the repository's base; it
  is never marked ready; it is closed before you finish.

Everything else a push or a change-request verb could do is still not yours.

**Every claim you make about the finished work is true of the tree as it finally
stands.** That is the property you are held to, and it says nothing about where your
report sits. This conversation does not end when you report — your supervisor keeps
asking, and answering well means running things — so a report required to be this
dispatch's literal final output is one no correct worker can give. What is required
instead is that nothing you have said about the work is untrue of the tree by the time you
stop.

When work follows your report, say in that same turn what changed and what you re-ran. A
correct delta satisfies this exactly as fully as restating the whole report does. Silence
does not satisfy it at all. Your last substantive turn should leave a reader able to say
what the finished tree contains and what was verified about it, whether that comes from
one report or from a report plus the deltas after it.

**A claim about a check, a test, a lint run, or a commit that was not run or was not made
is false, and fails on its merits.** A report asserting a check passed on a commit where
no such run occurred is that case, and one node of this host's history was correctly
failed for it. So do not carry a claim forward across a change that could have invalidated
it — re-run what the change could have broken, or say which claims you have not re-checked.

**Evidence deliberately about an earlier or induced state is not a false claim.** Proving
that an assertion can fail means making it fail, reading the message, and reverting;
proving that a message used to say nothing means quoting the run from before the change.
A citation of a run taken before a change, or of a failure induced on purpose as evidence,
is correct evidence — provided the citation says which it is. One node of this host was
failed for exactly that: its own criteria required its assertions be observed failing, and
the resulting-tree property above was read as forbidding the citation that requirement
produces.

**A commit that cannot affect a check leaves that check's evidence standing.** *Could have
invalidated it* is a condition, and a commit that fails it does not reach the claim — so a
run taken before a later commit is still evidence for the tree after it, provided the
report names that commit and says why it is inert for that check. What decides it is what
the check reads, never what kind of change the commit is. A comment-only or
documentation-only commit to content a check does not read is inert for that check; the
same comment is not inert for a check that reads comments, which a judged lint does, so
that one is re-run or named as not re-checked. A commit touching anything a check reads is
not inert for it, however small. Two dispatches of one node, about 45 minutes each, were
refused over nothing but a comment-only final commit after their cited check runs, with no
change in whether either tree was correct, and the manager had to send *re-run after every
commit* three separate times to get past it: read as absolute, the conditional rule above
is one no worker can meet, because every commit comes after the last run.

The ordering demand this replaces — that the report come after everything else, and that
anything found later be repaired and the whole report written again — is **withdrawn**. It
failed six of fourteen nodes in one workstream, each with complete committed work, a green
deterministic tier, and no acceptance criterion found unmet, and two of those carried an
escalated warning about it in their own task and failed anyway. A bar finished work
cannot clear teaches everyone to route around the thing that enforces quality; the
property above is what that demand was serving, and it is what survives.

### State the bar in `## Acceptance criteria`, not only here

A judge reads this node's `## Acceptance criteria` and its own review bar. Where the
criteria are silent about something the bar demands, it imports the demand and applies its
own reading of it — and finished, gate-green work has been failed twice that way: once for
running the gate's parts separately, and once for never having *"provided a final verified
completion report"*, a demand in neither the task nor the shared completion clause.

So every demand this node will be held to is stated as a criterion of its own, including
the two the bar makes of every implementation dispatch:

- the behavior this node adds is **proven end to end** by a test or journey that drives the
  real interface, rather than by inspection;
- every claim the dispatch makes about the finished work — what it verified, and the
  evidence for it — is **true of the tree as it finally stands**.

Criteria state properties of the finished tree; the commands that produce them belong in
this section. Whether the criteria answer every demand their own bar — or this appendix —
makes of them is read by `just review-plan <source:project>`, which spends a judged turn
on it and judges it by meaning: criteria that state a demand in their own words answer it,
and no criterion is refused for failing to use a particular phrase. Nothing reads it
deterministically any more, because the phrase matching that did refused wordings the same
review had just asked for.

OpenCode — anomalyco/opencode # OpenCode 社区动态日报（2026-07-05） ## 1) 今日速览 今天社区讨论的核心仍然是 **Windows 兼容性、更新/退出安全性、以及模型与平台适配问题**。同时，代码侧的 PR 主要集中在 **协议层事件流修正、MCP/工具链改造、以及 core/app 稳定性增强**，说明项目正在围绕“更稳的运行边界”持续收敛。 --- ## 2) 社区热点 Issues 1. **[#35327 `/exit` 会关闭父终端窗口（Windows）](https://github​.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/35327)** 这是典型的高风险行为：退出 opencode 竟然把整个宿主终端一起关掉，直接影响工作流连续性。该问题已有 3 条评论，说明社区对“进程隔离/控制台组行为”非常关注。 2. **[#35340 v1.17.13 Web UI 会话列表仍为空（稳定分支回归）](https://github​.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/35340)** 这是一个明确的回归问题，且涉及 stable 分支，影响面比单点 Bug 更大。评论中已经指向此前 dev 分支修复未回灌，说明社区在追踪“补丁是否正确回流”上反应积极。 3. **[#35334 Windows 安装器默认单用户安装](https://github​.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/35334)** 面向企业/IT 管理部署的场景，这个问题关系到安装路径、权限和可维护性。已有 2 条评论，表明桌面端的企业部署需求正在被放大。 4. **[#35331 NSIS 安装更新时会杀掉正在运行的 CLI 进程](https://github​.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/35331)** 这是非常严重的数据损失风险：更新桌面版时会误伤 CLI 会话。此类问题通常会优先级很高，因为它触及“更新安全”和“会话保留”。 5. **[#35330 Windows 上 `@​file` 自动补全路径异常](https://github​.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/35330)** 路径尾部反斜杠、分隔符不一致会直接导致文件解析失败，属于高频工作流 bug。评论数虽然不高，但这是典型的“影响广、复现稳定”的平台兼容问题。 6. **[#35329 Windows 文件监听器发出反斜杠路径](https://github​.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/35329)** 这类问题是路径规范化不一致的上游症状，会扩散到比较、缓存和触发逻辑。与 #35330 配合看，说明 Windows 路径栈是近期社区集中火力点。 7. **[#35365 1.17.12+ 之后自签名 TLS 证书失效](https://github​.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/35365)** 本地/内网 LLM 服务常依赖自签名证书，这个回归会直接打断企业和离线环境。社区反应偏“可用性优先”，说明本地部署兼容性很重要。 8. **[#35366 v1.17.13 在 OpenRouter 上生成会话标题失败](https://github​.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/35366)** 这个问题暴露出模型选择策略与具体 provider 约束之间的冲突，尤其是 reasoning mandatory 的 endpoint。它影响的是“自动化体验”，但背后是 provider 适配策略问题。 9. **[#35319 桌面端 RTL（阿拉伯语）渲染异常](https://github​.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/35319)** 这类国际化问题通常不会影响所有用户，但对多语言产品的完整性很关键。社区给出了“带修复方案”的提交方式，说明用户愿意推动国际化落地。 10. **[#35339 工作目录内容被 `rm -rf .` 删除且无确认](https://github​.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/35339)** 这是最高风险级别之一：缺少确认就执行破坏性命令。尽管评论数只有 2 条，但它直接触及 AI 工具最敏感的安全边界，值得重点盯防。 --- ## Epic #943. Inventory source #1010; only the selected Aperture/Layer expansion is in scope. Source inspected at [175581ee](https://github.com/jon-whiteroomsoftware/PXLBLZ-IDE/tree/175581eefb9281b3c90d07181150378fe1c04566). Paths below are locators at that commit; recheck ownership before implementation. AFK within the specified finite domain; a changed product guarantee or supported domain requires a named decision with Jon.

## What to build

Make “create a Layer, put these Clips on it, add another Pattern to it” a straightforward sequence through the existing production commands. The source already exposes `add_overlay_layer`, destination-aware `move_clip`, and `add_clip` with `overlay_layer_index`. This issue improves consistent addressing, useful receipts and production qualification. It does not add aliases such as create_layer/move_to_layer or rewrite the existing movement engine.

In one private operation, create the new Layer, move a plain Clip to it without changing its time, and add a Pattern at a specified free time. Commit once. Failed placement discards the entire private sequence, including the new Layer.

## Command design

### Existing `add_overlay_layer(zone_id)`

Keep its name, required Zone ID and behavior: create a fresh empty topmost overlay at index 0 in every composition Scene; previous Layers shift down. Retain the existing Group-shell preservation behavior, fresh-ID checks and per-Scene identity factory. Do not add arbitrary insertion position, custom Layer names, or a persistent unified-Layer ID.

Retain `targetId` and `details.layerIdsBySceneId` in its receipt. Add structured `details.zoneId` and `details.layer: 0`. Tool description states that a second creation shifts the first new Layer to index 1. New command invocations create new Layers; retransmitted identical deliveries reuse the original result through the existing delivery journal.

### Existing `add_clip`: consistent Layer argument

Add optional `layer` with existing descriptor kind `layer`: literal `main` or a nonnegative safe-integer overlay index. Both it and the existing `overlay_layer_index` are optional, but supplying both refuses as `invalid-argument`, even if values agree. Omit both to retain Main. Keep `overlay_layer_index` as a supported compatibility argument; describe `layer` as the preferred form for consistency with `move_clip`.

Resolve the chosen destination once into the existing ShowTimelineClipMoveTarget. Preserve current global-time rounding, default 5000 ms requested duration, fitting/clamping and `extend_show` behavior. Do not silently change add into exact-resize semantics. Missing Layer, occupied time and unsupported topology retain explicit refusal. Do not create a missing Layer implicitly.

Retain existing receipt target/instanceId. Add the actual result's `zoneId`, `layer`, `startMs`, `endMs`, `durationMs`; these report the resulting clamped/extended placement, not raw request numbers. Derive once from the accepted result or existing plan, reusing current projection/owner helpers. No private candidate snapshot in command receipts.

### Existing `move_clip`: Layer-only moves

Make `start_ms` optional at the descriptor boundary. Omission means retain the current logical Clip's start in the private candidate. At least one of `start_ms`, `zone_id`, or `layer` must be supplied. Supplied `start_ms` retains its current exact nonnegative safe-integer semantics; null is invalid. Retain current Zone/Layer defaults when those fields are omitted.

Resolve the current Clip's start through existing owner/projection code, then delegate to `moveShowClipExactly`. Keep that exact engine's request contract and collision/Transition checks; this convenience does not grant new topology support. The current record for a later command is the current private candidate, not the original begin_edit snapshot or the live Show.

A valid same-Layer/same-time request is a no-op. Unknown or Group-owned Clip, missing destination, occupied target, connected-chain destination change or visual Boundary Transition removal refuses atomically. Do not auto-detach Transitions, move neighbors, shift time, make Patterns independent, or retry another Layer. Receipts retain existing changed-Clip data and include actual selected Clip destination/time in structured details.

### Addressing convention

`main` is always Main. Overlay indices are zero-based, front-to-back, 0 topmost; they are positions in the current private candidate, not durable identities. Per-Scene Layer UUIDs and projected strings such as `zone:overlay:0` are not command indices. Use returned receipts plus the known preceding structural edits; do not read the live Show to recover uncommitted private changes. Existing begin_edit already captures the Show.

A manual insertion/reorder during the operation invalidates the existing whole-Show admission. Do not add a new token, cache or Layer-specific concurrency scheme. Within a private batch the caller explicitly accounts for index changes: after two top insertions the first new Layer is at 1. The existing transaction and journal enforce atomicity and replay protection.

## Limits

No new standalone read/list tools, Layer selector abstraction, names, blend modes or record schema. ShowOverlayLayer currently has id/name/placements and no configurable blend/mode field; do not infer one from the inventory. No bulk placement command, automatic packing, connected-chain migration to another Layer, Group authoring, destructive Layer cleanup or manual UI redesign. Existing supported Group-aware Layer creation remains available; direct Group-child moves remain refused.

## Implementation entry points

- `src/engine/showCommands/overlayLayer.ts`: existing descriptor and structured receipt.
- `src/engine/showCommands/clips.ts`: `addClipCommandOutcome`, add/move descriptors and move adapter; centralize only the argument-to-target resolution shared by these callers. Preserve current public names and compatibility.
- `src/engine/showCommands/support.ts`, `src/engine/showUnifiedTimelineProjection.ts`: existing Clip/Layer location and actual-result projection. A small shared Layer locator needed by later reorder/remove work may live here; do not prebuild a generalized selector system.
- `src/engine/showTimelineClipAuthoring.ts`: `addShowOverlayLayerAcrossTimeline`, `planShowClipAtGlobalTime`, existing add owners; `src/engine/showExactClipMove.ts`: existing exact move. Existing semantics should need little or no change.
- `src/engine/showCommands/descriptorSchema.ts`, `src/agent-harness/grammar/operations/descriptorAdapter.ts`, `src/worker/agent/builtinTools.ts` and `agentMcpRouting.ts`: derive changed schemas from descriptors. Canonical validation owns the mutually exclusive add arguments and at-least-one move argument; optional fields must remain optional in both transports.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A caller creates a Layer, moves a Clip there without resupplying its start, adds another Clip there, and commits one complete saved edit.
- [ ] `add_clip(layer:...)` and the old `overlay_layer_index` form produce equivalent records/receipts for the same destination; ambiguous dual arguments refuse.
- [ ] Existing time-fitting, extension, movement and topology restrictions remain unchanged, with actual destination/time receipts.
- [ ] Private sequence failure leaves no new Layer, moved Clip or partial save. Duplicate delivery creates no second Layer or Clip.
- [ ] Tool descriptions explain index direction and shifting, and production MCP/built-in schemas match the canonical fields.

## Tests

Use showOverlayLayerFixture and showCommandFixture with a second Zone/Scene and an existing linked instance; reuse existing IDs and deterministic factories.

- Move targeting: Main→overlay, overlay→Main, overlay→overlay and another Zone; omitted start preserves current time exactly. Same destination no-op; clip_id alone refuses. Existing exact start accepted/refused boundaries still pass.
- Connected destination change, Group child and visual Boundary Transition removal refuse without detachment; occupied destination refuses without moving neighbors. Existing same-Layer connected time moves remain supported. Preserve all logical segments, animation/Transition references and shared instance state.
- Sequence A: begin; add Layer; move Clip A there at its current start; add Pattern B later; commit. Compare complete document and exact target facts.
- Sequence B: create two Layers; move A to first-created index 1 and add B to second-created index 0. This catches stale-index reuse inside the batch.
- Sequence C: create Layer then request an occupied/invalid placement; private command refusal discards everything, including creation. Repeat a successful delivery with the same identity; one fresh-ID result and one eventual save. A wholly no-op move sequence never adopts.
- Stale live manual Layer insertion before commit refuses and preserves the manual edit. The new optional start resolves after a preceding successful private time move, so a Layer-only move does not restore an earlier start.
- Sparse Group-layer creation retains the existing #951 fixtures; no new uniform-stack restriction applies to this command family. New reorder/remove restrictions belong only to their tickets.
- Extend registry goldens/touch checks, shared parity rows, descriptor schema tests, built-in tool tests, production MCP tool listing and private-executor sequences. Add compact assertions for receipt identities and actual clamped durations. Mutation witnesses target ignored destination, defaulted/old start, a second creation on replay and lost Group-shell preservation only where existing catalogue coverage does not already detect them.

One production external MCP sequence through the bound live editor demonstrates create→move→add→commit, saved placement on the intended Layers, one Undo/Redo group and actual `.pxlshow` export/reopen equality. A repeated delivery does not repeat creation; an invalid final command and a concurrent manual Layer insertion produce no partial adoption. Extend an existing production seam once, shared with Aperture qualification; do not create a second admission framework. Reuse shared browser admission cases for lifecycle/save recovery instead of copying their setup. Existing manual Add/move/add owners supply parity; no new UI is required.

Focused convergence plus applicable worker schema/protocol tests and private executor cases must be included before final verification. Report source-qualified limitations separately from production proof. Screenshots are required only for gate-covered UI changes; record results as receipts/test references, not full-record evidence dumps.

None. Independent of the Aperture setter. Establish this convention before the new overlay reorder/remove commands; it can share their eventual Layer-family candidate.

Specified, not implemented. First-priority Layer workflow. Core create/add/move commands already exist; this issue authorizes only the above interface improvements and qualification, not their reimplementation.

Preserve `docs/reference/contracts/show-command-semantics.md` (typed refusal, exact declared writes, unrelated-field/order preservation and validated no-op), `show-state-history-persistence.md` (one adoption/history entry, durable save settlement/recovery), and `agent-candidate-application.md` plus `agent-oauth-discovery.md` (existing production private executor, session/revision admission and transport identity). Do not grant new Layer-scoped concurrency, retry, intermediate-invalid-state or hardware authority.

Keep the original `docs/plans/agent-show-command-census.md` as historical migration scope; link the new issue instead of rewriting its original 45-command promise. Regenerate affected capability reports honestly: direct editing is distinct from subtree preservation. Add examples and bounded unsupported cases to tool descriptions and current agent documentation. ## Delivery and evidence

This is a planned implementation issue, not an implementation claim. Use the current execution policy and reviewed-main workflow; worktree isolation and current committed-tip verification/review gates remain mandatory. Start with TDD and the named consumer cases. Reuse the existing descriptor projection, fixture builders, golden/touch/untouched-entity checks, parity rows and admission tests. Do not write a per-command adapter, new transaction framework, duplicate fixture suite, or evidence directory. Extend shared machinery only for an identified current need.

Issue granularity does not require one full delivery cycle per command. The Layer issues may form one family candidate with each issue's path scope and evidence identified; if delivered separately, land each reviewed tip before stacking further work. Keep aperture and Layer work independently deliverable. Freeze after focused checks; one coordinator owns required final-suite submission and exact-range review. No paid inference or hardware qualification is required to prove these deterministic command semantics. Diagnostic-only evidence cannot establish production MCP delivery.

# Security review — wallet: include txid in cold-signing output export

**Scope:** 2 files, +6/-2 lines · `src/wallet` (cold-signing output export/import, `exported_transfer_details` wire format)
**Boundaries:** hot(view)-wallet → cold-wallet output export blob and `unsigned_tx_set` (`import_outputs_from_str`, `sign_tx`); wallet cache persistence
**Result:** 3 findings: 1 MEDIUM, 2 LOW

## Findings

### [MEDIUM / CONFIRMED] Version-1 export data leaves `m_txid` uninitialized; the garbage is stored, persisted and published
- **Where:** `src/wallet/wallet2.h:288`, `src/wallet/wallet2.h:302-303`, `src/serialization/container.h:135`, `src/wallet/wallet2.cpp:14202`
- **Reach:** `import_outputs_from_str` → `::serialization::serialize(ar, new_outputs)` (`wallet2.cpp:14317`) → `do_serialize_container` → `exported_transfer_details e;` at `container.h:135` → `VERSION_FIELD` reads `version==1` → `if (version >= 2) FIELD(m_txid)` skipped → `import_outputs` → `td.m_txid = etd.m_txid` (`wallet2.cpp:14202`). Same via `sign_tx` → `import_outputs(exported_txs.new_transfers)` (`wallet2.cpp:7819-7820`), including the `unsigned_tx_set` v1 branch (`wallet2.h:476-481`).
- **Effect:** `container.h:135` *default*-initializes each element (`T e;`), not value-initializes. `exported_transfer_details` (`wallet2.h:264-305`) has no default member initializer and no user-provided constructor, and `crypto::hash` is `POD_CLASS hash { char data[32]; }` (`crypto/hash.h:47-49`, `common/pod-class.h:33`, `POD_CLASS` = `struct`). For version-1 input `m_txid` is therefore never written and holds indeterminate stack bytes, which `wallet2.cpp:14202` copies into `transfer_details::m_txid` — including for entries the loop then `continue`s over, since the assignment precedes the already-imported check at `wallet2.cpp:14216-14228`. That value is persisted to the wallet cache (`wallet2_basic/wallet2_serialization.h:63`), printed by `incoming_transfers` (`simplewallet.cpp:5882`), returned by the `incoming_transfers` RPC (`wallet_rpc_server.cpp:2291`, now taking the non-`null_hash` branch), fed to `hash_m_transfer` (`wallet2.cpp:15341`, so `finish_rescan_bc_keep_key_images` becomes nondeterministic) and embedded in reserve proofs (`wallet2.cpp:12475`). Version-1 is the format every currently released hot wallet emits, so this is the compatibility path the PR description says it preserves.
- **Magnitude corrected down from the first pass:** it is one stack slot, not 32 bytes *per output* — `e` is reconstructed at the same address each iteration and nothing in the v1 field list writes `m_txid`, so every imported transfer receives the same indeterminate 32 bytes. The only outward publication is a reserve proof, which is already invalid from a cold wallet; the rest is UB plus local disclosure in a process holding the spend key. Severity stays MEDIUM on the strength of the uninitialized read reaching persisted state on the default path, not on the leak volume.
- **Verification:** attacked it as a value-initialization claim — `do_serialize_container` (`container.h:132-141`) constructs with `T e;` and `do_add(v, std::move(e))`, so no `resize`-style zeroing occurs; and the epee `struct_init` zeroing described in `macros.md` does not apply, this is the `BEGIN_SERIALIZE_OBJECT` binary serializer. Before this PR every field was read unconditionally, so the indeterminate bytes were always overwritten.
- **Fix:** `crypto::hash m_txid{};` at `wallet2.h:288`, or `else m_txid = crypto::null_hash;` on the `version >= 2` branch.

### [LOW / CONFIRMED] Cold wallet now stores and displays a txid the untrusted hot wallet chose, and the change breaks the existing test
- **Where:** `src/wallet/wallet2.cpp:14202`
- **Effect:** in cold signing the view wallet is untrusted (`wallet2.cpp:7845`, `wallet2.cpp:7871` — `ptx.tx_key = rct::rct2sk(rct::identity()); // don't send it back to the untrusted view wallet`). `import_outputs` verifies the output pubkey against the derived ephemeral key (`wallet2.cpp:14263-14264`) but performs no check on `m_txid`, and `td.m_tx` is a synthetic prefix (`wallet2.cpp:14233-14241`), so the value is unverifiable offline by construction. The air-gapped wallet then presents an attacker-chosen hash as authoritative (`simplewallet.cpp:5882`, `wallet_rpc_server.cpp:2291`) and copies it into reserve proofs (`wallet2.cpp:12475`). The previous `crypto::null_hash` was deliberate: commit `a760393d` is titled "wallet_rpc_server: leave unknown incoming tx hash empty", and `tests/functional_tests/cold_signing.py:150` asserts `cold_transfers_list[i]['tx_hash'] == ''` — which this change breaks and the PR does not update.
- **Verification:** checked for any cross-check of the txid on the cold side — `import_outputs` compares only `m_internal_output_index` and `m_pubkey` when deciding to reprocess (`wallet2.cpp:14219-14224`). The red `Ubuntu 24.04 (tests)` check on this head is the job that runs `ctest` including the functional suite (`.github/workflows/build.yml:200-252`), and `cold_signing` is in the functional test list (`tests/functional_tests/functional_tests_rpc.py:14`).
- **Fix:** drop the field, or gate acceptance on the cold wallet being able to verify it; at minimum update `cold_signing.py:150` and state the trust-model change.

### [LOW / CONFIRMED] Wire format changed without bumping `OUTPUT_EXPORT_FILE_MAGIC`, so an old wallet reports success on a rejected import
- **Where:** `src/wallet/wallet2.cpp:137` (`OUTPUT_EXPORT_FILE_MAGIC "Monero output export\004"`), `src/wallet/wallet2.cpp:117` (`UNSIGNED_TX_PREFIX "...\005"`)
- **Effect:** the magic still matches (`wallet2.cpp:14278-14281`), so an unpatched cold wallet reads `version==2`, passes `if (version < 1)`, stops before `m_txid`, and leaves 32 bytes per element unconsumed. Both parse attempts then fail `check_stream_state` (`wallet2.cpp:14319`, `14331`) and `import_outputs_from_str` returns `0` without throwing (`wallet2.cpp:14343`), so `simplewallet` prints `"0 outputs imported"` through `success_msg_writer` (`simplewallet.cpp:10088-10089`). In an air-gapped flow the user gets no signal that the import was rejected for a version reason.
- **Verification:** attacked this as a possible silent-corruption bug instead of a silent-zero one. On the `sign_tx` side `parse_unsigned_tx_from_str` has no `check_stream_state` (`wallet2.cpp:7778-7791`), so a *single*-element `new_transfers` would parse and import correctly with the txid bytes ignored; multi-element input desynchronises, and any resulting garbage is caught by `THROW_WALLET_EXCEPTION_IF(in_ephemeral.pub != out_key, ...)` at `wallet2.cpp:14263`. So the failure mode really is the silent zero, not corruption. Dropped the first pass's "the magic was bumped to `\004` when the compact format was introduced" precedent: settling it needs `git log -S`, which does not complete cheaply here, and the finding does not rest on it.
- **Fix:** bump `OUTPUT_EXPORT_FILE_MAGIC` to `\005` (and `UNSIGNED_TX_PREFIX` to `\006`), or make `import_outputs_from_str` throw when no parse succeeds.

## Refuted
- ~~Privacy regression in decoy/input selection via `get_output_relatedness`~~ — `wallet2.cpp:7444` compares `m_txid`, but the only callers are tx-construction paths that need a daemon, and `import_outputs` throws for any wallet that has refreshed (`wallet2.cpp:14175-14176`).
- ~~New information leak in the export blob~~ — the blob is encrypted with the view secret key (`wallet2.cpp:14088`), and any holder of that key already knows the txid.
- ~~Forged reserve proof via attacker-chosen `proof.txid`~~ — `check_reserve_proof` fetches each tx by that txid from the daemon (`wallet2.cpp:12604-12613`) and re-derives the output key and key image, so a wrong txid makes the proof fail, not pass.
- ~~Buffer overrun from the added 32 bytes~~ — `FIELD(crypto::hash)` is a fixed 32-byte blob (`crypto/hash.h:47-49`); no attacker-chosen length is introduced.
- ~~First pass's claim that commit `a760393d`'s rationale was unreadable~~ — `git log --no-walk --format='%B' a760393d` returns it ("wallet_rpc_server: leave unknown incoming tx hash empty"); only `git show`'s diff blob is unfetchable. Folded into the LOW finding above.

## Checked and clear
- Signing path unaffected: `sign_tx` never reads `m_txid`; it uses `sd.sources`/`sd.selected_transfers` only. `wallet2.cpp:7816-7877`
- `unsigned_tx_set` version dispatch (`VERSION_FIELD(2)`, v0/v1 branches) is unchanged and still routes v1 payloads through the same `exported_transfer_details` reader. `wallet2.h:462-484`
- Key-image export/import (`KEY_IMAGE_EXPORT_FILE_MAGIC` path) does not carry `m_txid` and is untouched. `wallet2.cpp:13103`, `13190`
- No consensus, P2P, RPC-daemon or RingCT code is reached — the change is confined to two wallet files.
- `exported_transfer_details` appears nowhere outside `wallet2.h`/`wallet2.cpp` (grep over `src/` and `tests/`), so no test covers its cross-version round trip; the only test on this surface is `tests/functional_tests/cold_signing.py`, broken by the change.
- The `Debian 11` CI failure is not attributable to this diff: that matrix job builds only and has no test step (`.github/workflows/build.yml:148-198`), and every other build job on this head is green.

## Not covered
- The upstream `Ubuntu 24.04 (tests)` log was not retrievable from this checkout, so the match between the red check and `cold_signing.py:150` is derived from the code and the test registration, not from the failure output.

Pi — badlogic/pi-mono # Pi 社区动态日报 · 2026-09-13 ## 今日速览 今日社区活跃度集中在 TUI 交互细节优化与多 Provider OAuth 接入两条主线上：fullscreen 模式下的滚轮/选区问题、keybinding 可配置化、OAuth 回调渲染扩展成为高频讨论焦点；同时 `openai-codex` 连接可靠性这一"老大难"问题（#4945，78 评论、33 👍）持续推进，标记为 inprogress。多个新 PR 已合并落地，包括人类可读的模型标签、工具调用合并渲染、loop-guard 示例扩展等。 ## 版本发布 过去 24 小时无新 Release。 ## 社区热点 Issues 1. **[#4945](https://github​.com/earendil-works/pi-mono/issues/4945) — openai-codex 连接可靠性问题（inprogress）** `gpt-5.5` / `openai-codex` 频繁出现 TUI 卡在 `Working...`、无流式输出、无错误提示，只能 Esc 中断。社区互动量最高（78 评论、33 👍），是当前最阻塞生产环境的稳定性问题，与 transport 层心跳保活、idle timeout 相关。 2. **[#9052](https://github​.com/earendil-works/pi-mono/issues/9052) — Fullscreen 滚轮滚动比普通模式慢约 3 倍** Fullscreen 模式锁定输入框的体验得到认可，但滚轮性能明显劣化，影响长会话阅读体验。 3. **[#8928](https://github​.com/earendil-works/pi-mono/issues/8928) — 并行启动时 OAuth 过期凭证导致 ~48s "No API key found"（inprogress）** 当 `auth.json` 中存在其他 Provider 的过期 OAuth 凭证时，多进程启动会以错误 Provider 为靶点报密钥缺失。作者给出了确定性复现与耗时数据。 4. **[#9311](https://github​.com/earendil-works/pi-mono/issues/9311) — Fullscreen 模式下选中文本在会话切换后残留** 选区状态未在切换/新建会话时清理，导致内容被错误带入新会话。 5. **[#5372](https://github​.com/earendil-works/pi-mono/issues/5372) — 允许自定义 OAuth 回调页渲染** 当前 `oauthSuccessHtml/oauthErrorHtml` 写死 `renderPage`，扩展/嵌入式集成方希望接管浏览器最终页样式。 6. **[#9098](https://github​.com/earendil-works/pi-mono/issues/9098) — 在 RPC 响应中暴露 prompt disposition** 建议在 `prompt` 成功响应中加入 `data.disposition: "handled" | "queued" | "started"`，便于扩展/SDK 区分"已消费 vs 已入队 vs 已开始"。 7. **[#5365](https://github​.com/earendil-works/pi-mono/issues/5365) — bun 安装后底层仍跑 node（已关闭）** `pi` 通过 bun 全局安装后运行时报 `markAsUncloneable` 错误，底层实际调用了 node 的 undici。已关闭，需关注后续修复是否回归。 8. **[#9267](https://github​.com/earendil-works/pi-mono/issues/9267) — 降低 fuzzyMatch 的逐字符扫描成本** 提议将 `fuzzy.ts` 内的循环替换为 `String.indexOf()`，在不改变排序的前提下提升会话搜索性能。 9. **[#9243](https://github​.com/earendil-works/pi-mono/issues/9243) — 会话恢复时模型被 echo 名称覆盖** Provider 回显的模型名若与路由 id 不同，`getSessionContextSettings` 会错误地用前者覆盖 model，造成"恢复即换模型"。 10. **[#7629](https://github​.com/earendil-works/pi-mono/issues/7629) — `tui.select.pageUp/pageDown` 并非在所有列表中生效** 键盘无 PageUp/PageDown 时通过 keybinding 重映射，发现部分选择器未消费该事件，行为不一致。 ## 重要 PR 进展 1. **[#9541](https://github​.com/earendil-works/pi-mono/pull/9541) — fix(tui): 显示人类可读的模型标签（已合并）** 在 `/model` 等选择器中将模型 `name` 作为主标签、id 降为副信息，治理目录中已具备 friendly name。 2. **[#9539](https://github​.com/earendil-works/pi-mono/pull/9539) — examples: 新增 loop-guard 扩展示例（已合并）** 检测并打断"重复同一工具调用"的 LLM agent 死循环，例如 `curl` 一直返回非零导致模型反复重试。 3. **[#9096](https://github​.com/earendil-works/pi-mono/pull/9096) — feat(ai,coding-agent): 新增 Meta + Muse 订阅 OAuth（OPEN）** 解决 #7543，典型 sub provider，但有两点特殊：refresh token 改为基于 identity token 每日重新铸造；当前 streaming 是"伪流式"（整段 burst 输出）。 4. **[#9531](https://github​.com/earendil-works/pi-mono/pull/9531) — feat(tree): 会话树支持永久删除分支（已合并）** 新增 `SessionManager.pruneBranch(entryId)` + `countSubtree()`，保护活跃路径与叶子节点，重新链接标签与 compaction；`/tree` 中 `shift+d` 触发删除。 5. **[#9529](https://github​.com/earendil-works/pi-mono/pull/9529) — feat(ai): 新增 Google Antigravity 和 Cursor Pro OAuth（已合并）** 两个订阅型、无需 API Key 的 OAuth Provider；Antigravity 对接 `accounts.google.com` (Cloud Code Assist)，本地回调端口 51123，支持手动 code 回退。 6. **[#8635](https://github​.com/earendil-works/pi-mono/pull/8635) — fix(ai): lazy setup 期间保留 aborted 停止原因（OPEN）** 修复 #8409：将 abort signal 透传到 lazy stream setup 包装器；setup 失败时若请求已被中止，按 aborted 报告，并补回归测试。 7. **[#9523](https://github​.com/earendil-works/pi-mono/pull/9523) — 修复 Pi 自有阻塞提示未触发 ui_prompt_start/_end（已合并）** 模型选择器、设置、resume、session tree 等内置选择器经 `showSelector()` 走通后不再沉默，状态集成方（如"等待用户"上报）可看到完整事件。 8. **[#9517](https://github​.com/earendil-works/pi-mono/pull/9517) — feat(tui): 折叠长工具调用链（已合并）** 将连续 6 次以上的同类工具调用折叠为一行汇总展示，失败调用仍可展开，含渲染测试。 9. **[#9514](https://github​.com/earendil-works/pi-mono/pull/9514) — fix(tui): 将硬编码快捷键改为可配置 keybinding（已合并）** 编辑器/输入框/模型选择器内的快捷键统一走 keybinding，新增 Ctrl+C 清空搜索/取消模型选择等回归测试。 10. **[#9540](https://github​.com/earendil-works/pi-mono/pull/9540) — coding-agent: extension loader 延后加载 jiti 与 TUI 图（已关闭）** 把 `core/extensions/loader.ts` 中 `jiti/static` 与虚拟模块表的 import 推迟到首个扩展加载时，便于 SDK 嵌入场景减少启动开销。 ## 功能需求趋势 - **TUI 体验打磨**：fullscreen 模式的滚轮性能（#9052）、选区残留（#9311）、ScrollView 鼠标事件转发（#9538）、人类可读模型标签（#9541）、keybinding 可配置化（#9514）、长工具调用折叠（#9517）—— 多个 PR/Issue 联动推进。 - **多 Provider OAuth 生态扩张**：新增 Meta Muse（#9096）、Google Antigravity + Cursor Pro（#9529/#9530），同时推动回调页可定制（#5372）；社区明显希望降低 API Key 依赖、拥抱订阅型登录。 - **Codex / OpenAI 传输稳定性**：#4945（连接挂死）、#9474（per-request 总 deadline 缺失）、#9481（turn-attribution 元数据对齐）、#9013（缓存提示误报）形成一簇聚焦。 - **性能与可观测性**：fuzzy 搜索扫描成本（#9267）、扩展加载时机（#9540）、流式 UI 首 token 重复渲染（#9542）、session 搜索/排序。 - **会话管理增强**：模型恢复正确性（#9243）、resume 列表内 fork 快捷键（#9521）、会话树分支删除（#9531）、compaction 预算支持窗口比例（#9415）。 - **SDK 嵌入友好性**：自定义 `agentDir` 下的 `/login` 状态行（#9537）、ui_prompt 事件覆盖（#9522/#9523）。 ## 开发者关注点 - **痛点 1：Codex 长会话断流与超时**。#4945 持续位于榜首，#9474 进一步指出无不可重置的 per-request wall-clock deadline，被周期性事件绕过，反映出对生产可用性的强烈诉求。 - **痛点 2：Fullscreen TUI 体验不一致**。滚轮慢、选区残留、ScrollView 鼠标丢失三连击 (#9052/#9311/#9538)，说明 fullscreen 作为"日常主模式"被越来越多用户采用，但其交互完整性仍有明显缺口。 - **痛点 3：跨 Provider 缓存/模型提示误报**。#9013（vLLM 误报 cache miss）、#9243（模型名被 echo 覆盖）、#9512（GPT-6 Astra max reasoning 触顶 compaction）显示在多模型混用场景下，状态提示与缓存语义需要更精细的边界处理。 - **痛点 4：扩展与 SDK 嵌入的启动成本/事件覆盖**。#9540 关注 import 时机，#9522/#9523 关注内置 UI 事件的可观测性，#9537 关注自定义 agentDir 下的状态显示；嵌入式集成方越来越希望把 Pi 当作"库"而非 CLI 使用。 - **高频需求：可配置化与可扩展性**。从 OAuth 回调渲染 (#5372)、keybinding 可配置 (#9514)、模型选择器 UI 改进 (#9541/#9536 working visibility override) 看，社区共识是"Pi 应提供默认体验，同时允许在每个交互细节上被替换"。

### Issue Type

Refactoring

### Description

Native tool selection, capability filtering, schema construction, and rebuilding are implemented separately across nodes and the CLI. The same tool configuration can expose different tools or schemas depending on the entry point, and rebuilding can expand the originally selected tool set.

This is the broader follow-up to the investigation of #1392 and [nightly run 33994384699](https://github.com/Datus-ai/Datus-agent/actions/runs/33994384699). The narrow `query_metrics` registration/schema regression is being handled separately; this issue tracks the remaining inconsistencies and consolidation work.

### Context and observed behavior

Baseline: `cc9d64816f77debd87b07e530a7cf9f1bc9d25e9` on `upstream/main`, inspected on 2026-09-06.

| Area | Current behavior | Expected behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GenSQL rebuild | With `tools: db_tools.list_tables`, `_rebuild_tools()` adds the entire available DB group, including `execute_sql`. | Rebuilds preserve the original selection and explicitly declared required tools. |
| DB schema binding | With `catalog` unsupported, named `list_tables` registration omits it in GenSQL but exposes it in GenReport and BaseVisualArtifact. Those paths bypass `DBFuncTool.to_function_tool()`. | Every entry point applies the same capability-dependent schema rules. |
| Named selection | Several nodes check `hasattr()` and convert the method directly. An isolated provider advertising no available tools can still have its method mounted by GenReport. | Named and wildcard selection share capability checks; method existence alone is insufficient. |
| Chat configuration | `tools: db_tools.list_tables` selects the entire DB family by design in `_selected_tool_families()`. | Give explicit method selection consistent semantics. Tightening Chat's existing behavior needs a documented compatibility change. |
| CLI ServiceClient | Enumeration keeps only names from `available_tools()`, then `get_tool()` reconstructs wrappers. Enumeration errors fall back to method existence. | Listing and invocation share the correctly bound tools without discarding schema/capability decisions. |

The first four observations were checked with small Python probes invoking the existing registration/rebuild methods. The DB schema probe used real DB methods and the real converter with a controlled unsupported-`catalog` capability condition; other probes used minimal provider doubles. These establish registration behavior, not full database/LLM execution results.

Code pointers:

- [GenSQL rebuild](https://github.com/Datus-ai/Datus-agent/blob/cc9d64816f77debd87b07e530a7cf9f1bc9d25e9/datus/agent/node/gen_sql_agentic_node.py#L216), [named registration](https://github.com/Datus-ai/Datus-agent/blob/cc9d64816f77debd87b07e530a7cf9f1bc9d25e9/datus/agent/node/gen_sql_agentic_node.py#L449).
- [DB schema factory](https://github.com/Datus-ai/Datus-agent/blob/cc9d64816f77debd87b07e530a7cf9f1bc9d25e9/datus/tools/func_tool/database.py#L1186), [GenReport registration](https://github.com/Datus-ai/Datus-agent/blob/cc9d64816f77debd87b07e530a7cf9f1bc9d25e9/datus/agent/node/gen_report_agentic_node.py#L258), [visual artifact registration](https://github.com/Datus-ai/Datus-agent/blob/cc9d64816f77debd87b07e530a7cf9f1bc9d25e9/datus/agent/node/base_visual_artifact_agentic_node.py#L313).
- [Chat family selection](https://github.com/Datus-ai/Datus-agent/blob/cc9d64816f77debd87b07e530a7cf9f1bc9d25e9/datus/agent/node/chat_agentic_node.py#L141), [CLI enumeration and binding](https://github.com/Datus-ai/Datus-agent/blob/cc9d64816f77debd87b07e530a7cf9f1bc9d25e9/datus/cli/service_client.py#L95).

Additional duplication to consolidate:

- AskReport/AskDashboard build the Chat tool set, filter it afterward, and repeat that filtering after rebuilds.
- Startup setup and lazy bash/skill/memory/web injection are separate assembly paths. Visual artifact tools are also added immediately before execution.
- Some `all_tools_name()` implementations discover public methods and exclude helpers with handwritten lists. API catalogs, actual mounted tools, and permission metadata must remain consistent without treating every public method as an exposed tool.

Related: #929 covers database namespace interpretation and unsupported namespace fields. This issue focuses on consistently applying tool selection and binding rules across consumers.

### Proposed Solution

1. Declare each tool's binding/schema rules, capability conditions, and default exposure at its tool group. Distinguish **defined**, **currently available**, **included by default**, and **selected for this consumer**.
2. Introduce a shared instance-scoped catalog/resolver for `group`, `group.*`, and `group.method`. Reuse the existing converter and permission infrastructure; migrate consumers and delete their duplicate branches.
3. Use one assembly lifecycle for initial setup, repeated setup, datasource changes, and runtime additions. Nodes declare defaults, required tools, and context such as read-only mode and filesystem roots.
4. Have CLI listing and invocation consume the same bound tool objects, retaining its read-method allowlist.
5. Derive name/category metadata from the same definitions. The existing `ToolRegistry` is a permission lookup, potentially containing a superset of mounted names; it must not become the authority for which tools are exposed.

Migration constraints:

- Preserve GenJob's explicitly selected transfer/migration tools without adding them to every node's default DB wildcard set.
- Preserve empty tool whitelists and artifact scope for AskReport/AskDashboard. Creating an internal DB/filesystem dependency must not automatically expose its tools.
- Represent node-local/stateful tools and intentional replacements explicitly; preserve existing permission categories and state callbacks.
- Preserve proxy/transformer/permission behavior and rebuild their bindings correctly. Do not share mutable bound tools across nodes, users, or datasources, or lose stateful plan/artifact objects on unrelated rebuilds.
- Keep node-specific absent/empty defaults explicit. Record Chat's method-selection tightening separately from mechanical refactoring.
- Retain protocol boundaries for MCP and provider-native tools; they need not become Agents FunctionTools.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] With the same capabilities and context, named, wildcard, CLI, and rebuild paths produce consistent schemas, strictness, parameter exclusions, and invocation behavior.
- [ ] `db_tools.list_tables` remains limited to that selection plus declared required tools after repeated setup and datasource switches; changed datasource capabilities are reflected consistently.
- [ ] Named selection cannot bypass capability checks or expose internal helpers; unknown selections and schema construction failures produce actionable diagnostics.
- [ ] Explicit-only GenJob tools remain available where requested without expanding default tool sets.
- [ ] Empty artifact-ask whitelists, read-only modes, internal-only dependencies, and node-specific defaults remain covered.
- [ ] Rebuilds preserve correct permission categories, proxy behavior, and policy transformers without stale or duplicate wrappers; conflicting tool names are detected.
- [ ] Deterministic tests use real schema conversion and actual registration/invocation paths, run in ordinary PR tests and the nightly unit stage, and do not depend on an LLM choosing a particular tool.
- [ ] Migrated consumers no longer maintain parallel selection/conversion branches or permanent fallback paths.

The official `v1.2.937-nightly` source contains both the counter reset and Standard-to-AppendOnly optimization described below. The official `v1.2.833-nightly` snapshot type has no `logical_change_counters` field.

**Evidence boundary:** the full failure was observed in the cross-version CI matrix of #20079 (current Query commit `67899d03863186fa1085c9e7790059b9e180cd37` alternating with `1.2.833`). A focused test using the real snapshot constructors also reproduced the counter discontinuity. The simplified two-official-release SQL sequence below has not yet been independently executed end-to-end. It is a reproduction recipe derived from the verified code path, not a claim of a completed official-release binary test.

### What's Wrong?

A Standard Stream can be incorrectly optimized into AppendOnly after a counter-aware Query writes data, a legacy Query publishes a snapshot without logical change counters, and a counter-aware Query publishes another snapshot.

The missing counters are initialized as zero. If the Stream's base snapshot also has zero UPDATE/DELETE counters, the endpoints appear to have no updates/deletes, even though those operations occurred before the legacy writer dropped the counters.

This can silently omit DELETE rows and UPDATE pairs from Standard Stream results. It does not require concurrent mixed-version nodes: sequential downgrade/write/upgrade is sufficient to create the relevant history.

#### Observed CI failure

[Failing compatibility job](https://github.com/databendlabs/databend/actions/runs/34597602981/job/103274287832)

File: `tests/compat_fuse/compat-logictest/granule_index_mixed/04_old_current_final/fuse_compat_read.test:45`

```sql
SELECT change$action, change$is_update, count()
FROM gi_s
GROUP BY change$action, change$is_update;
```

Expected:

```text
DELETE false   3
DELETE true   11
INSERT false 310
INSERT true   11
```

Actual:

```text
INSERT false 310
```

The earlier current-version read in `02_old_current_merge` returned all four categories correctly. The later legacy writer published new snapshots, then the current reader executed `RECLUSTER FINAL` before the failing Stream query.

### How to Reproduce?

Use an isolated Linux environment, not production data. Download official Query binaries from the [1.2.937 release](https://github.com/databendlabs/databend/releases/tag/v1.2.937-nightly) and [1.2.833 release](https://github.com/databendlabs/databend/releases/tag/v1.2.833-nightly).

Keep the same Meta, tenant ID, and persistent storage path across Query restarts. Stop one Query before starting the other. Do not clear snapshots, recreate the Stream, or consume the Stream using a write statement between stages. If a deployment requires a license for the relevant features, use a valid test license.

This sequence does not use granule indexes, virtual columns, or branch-specific recluster settings. INSERT is used to guarantee that the last new-version operation publishes a snapshot.

#### 1. Query 1.2.937: create a Standard Stream, then update and delete

```sql
SELECT version();
CREATE DATABASE stream_counter_repro;
USE stream_counter_repro;

CREATE TABLE t(id INT, value STRING) change_tracking = true;
INSERT INTO t VALUES (1, 'one'), (2, 'two'), (3, 'three');
CREATE STREAM s ON TABLE t APPEND_ONLY = false;

SELECT count() FROM s; -- 0

UPDATE t SET value = 'one_updated' WHERE id = 1;
DELETE FROM t WHERE id = 2;

SELECT change$action, change$is_update, count()
FROM s
GROUP BY change$action, change$is_update
ORDER BY change$action, change$is_update;
```

Correct result:

```text
DELETE false 1
DELETE true  1
INSERT true  1
```

The Stream base counters are `(0, 0)`; the latest counters after the mutations are `(1, 1)`.

#### 2. Stop Query 1.2.937; start Query 1.2.833 on the same data

```sql
SELECT version();
USE stream_counter_repro;
INSERT INTO t VALUES (4, 'four');
SELECT id, value FROM t ORDER BY id;
```

Expected table data:

```text

3 three
4 four
```

The old writer publishes a snapshot without `logical_change_counters`.

#### 3. Stop Query 1.2.833; start Query 1.2.937 again

First query the Stream **before any new write**:

```sql
SELECT version();
USE stream_counter_repro;

SELECT change$action, change$is_update, count()
FROM s
GROUP BY change$action, change$is_update
ORDER BY change$action, change$is_update;
```

At this checkpoint, the missing latest counters should cause the optimizer to retain Standard mode. Expected:

```text
DELETE false 1
DELETE true  1
INSERT false 1
INSERT true  1
```

If this checkpoint already fails, investigate an additional compatibility problem rather than attributing it solely to the reset below.

Now publish a new snapshot using the new version:

```sql
INSERT INTO t VALUES (5, 'five');

SELECT id, value FROM t ORDER BY id;
-- 1 one_updated
-- 3 three
-- 4 four
-- 5 five

SELECT change$action, change$is_update, count()
FROM s
GROUP BY change$action, change$is_update
ORDER BY change$action, change$is_update;
```

Correct result:

```text
DELETE false 1
DELETE true  1
INSERT false 2
INSERT true  1
```

Predicted incorrect result from the verified reset/optimization path:

```text
INSERT false 2
```

### Root cause evidence

In [TableSnapshot::try_new, official 1.2.937 source](https://github.com/databendlabs/databend/blob/v1.2.937-nightly/src/query/storages/common/table_meta/src/meta/v4/snapshot.rs#L175-L180):

```rust
let logical_change_counters = Some(
    prev_snapshot
        .as_ref()
        .and_then(|snapshot| snapshot.logical_change_counters)
        .unwrap_or_default(),
);
```

This conflates a new history with no predecessor and an existing history whose counters are unknown. A current-version descendant of a legacy snapshot receives `Some((0, 0))`.

In [optimize_stream_mode, official 1.2.937 source](https://github.com/databendlabs/databend/blob/v1.2.937-nightly/src/query/storages/fuse/src/operations/changes.rs#L241-L264):

```rust
if logical_change_delta(Some(&base_snapshot), Some(&latest_snapshot))?
    .is_some_and(|delta| delta == (0, 0))
{
    Ok(StreamMode::AppendOnly)
}
```

The original base `(0, 0)` and reset latest `(0, 0)` are compared as if their counters belonged to a continuous history.

A focused local test constructed this sequence using `TableSnapshot::try_from_previous()` and simulated a legacy serialization by removing the counter field:

- Base `(0, 0)`, after mutations `(11, 3)`: delta is `Some((11, 3))`.
- Legacy latest with the field removed: delta is `None`, as expected.
- Current child of that legacy snapshot: counters become `(0, 0)` and delta becomes `Some((0, 0))`, incorrectly qualifying for AppendOnly.

Both relevant code paths come from #20160 (`0fd0d51677`), not the virtual-column/granule changes in #20079. Pure upstream end-to-end binary reproduction is still needed to complete the validation above.

### Expected behavior / fix considerations

Unknown or discontinuous counters must not prove that no UPDATE/DELETE occurred. Preserve Standard Stream semantics and fall back to endpoint/origin-based processing when continuity cannot be established.

Possible approaches include preserving unknown counters across descendants of legacy snapshots, or recording a counter-history identity and comparing only endpoints from the same history. Also review `add_logical_change_delta()`, transaction retry handling, backlog estimates, and changes-table statistics so another path does not turn unknown history into trusted zero counters.

A decreasing-counter check alone cannot catch this case: the observed problematic endpoint values are zero on both sides.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Save the DGD above as `deployment.yaml`, resolve the placement/cache placeholders, and use an existing namespace, model-cache PVC, and HF secret.
2. Deploy and wait for readiness:

   ```bash
   kubectl -n "$NAMESPACE" apply --dry-run=server -f deployment.yaml
   ```

3. In another terminal, confirm `GET /v1/models` contains `Qwen/Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-1.7B-CustomVoice`, then send the request below. The exact saved request was replayed unchanged for the observed September 10 rerun.

Save as `request.json`:

```json
{
  "input": "Hey, this is generated using NVIDIA Dynamo.",
  "model": "Qwen/Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-1.7B-CustomVoice",
  "voice": "vivian",
  "language": "English",
  "data_source": "b64_json",
  "response_format": "wav"
}
```

```bash
curl --max-time 1200 -sS -D headers.txt \
  http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/audio/speech \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data-binary @request.json -o output.wav
```

## Expected behavior

A complete WAV containing the requested utterance, or a correctly implemented streaming response preserving all audio chunks. The returned waveform must not consist solely of an initial silent chunk.

## Actual behavior

- HTTP **200**, `Content-Type: audio/wav`.
- Exactly **3,884 bytes**, mono 16-bit PCM, 24 kHz, 1,920 frames: **0.08 s**.
- RMS **0**, peak **0**, **0 nonzero samples**.
- SHA-256 `056e096196265b3e34608224a2e81e7c607daf5cadb366f5cd84d00c302b3350`, identical to the earlier failed run.
- For that same HTTP request, worker logs record three WAV chunks:

  ```text
  1920 samples, sr=24000, 3884 bytes wav
  48000 samples, sr=24000, 96044 bytes wav
  40320 samples, sr=24000, 80684 bytes wav
  ```

  That is 3.76 s of encoded worker output, but only the first 0.08 s reaches the HTTP caller.

A separate direct-to-worker request captured all three chunks: 0.08 s silent, 2.00 s non-silent, 0.72 s non-silent (2.80 s total). Its first chunk is byte-identical to the HTTP output. This proves subsequent worker audio exists; **it is not an end-to-end HTTP pass or a listening/transcription claim**.

**Important correction to the earlier umbrella report:** raw WAV is the intended frontend response here, even with `data_source=b64_json`. The absence of a JSON/base64 envelope is not the bug. Selecting only the first WAV is.

## Diagnosis and suggested scope

The [1.4.2 frontend speech handler](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/blob/v1.4.2/lib/llm/src/http/service/openai.rs) folds the response stream, then selects `response.data.first()` and decodes only that item's base64 into the HTTP body. The [audio aggregator](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/blob/v1.4.2/lib/llm/src/protocols/openai/audios/aggregator.rs) extends the data list; it does not concatenate complete waveform payloads into that first entry.

[PR #12100](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/12100), commit `a97afd2d51819f88d1033522312137b35feabc9d`, merged speech-streaming/compatibility work. It is present on the tested example branch but is **not an ancestor of tag v1.4.2**. Include the appropriate frontend and worker changes in matched images, then rerun this case. If backporting is not appropriate, explicitly document which image/release revision is required rather than marking the stock 1.4.2 DGD as working.

This is **not a missing CLI flag**: `--trust-remote-code`, `--enforce-eager`, and `VLLM_ALLOW_LONG_MAX_MODEL_LEN=1` were already aligned with the launcher and present in the tested deployment.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The versioned support boundary is explicit: validated fixed images or a clearly documented limitation/backport decision for 1.4.2.
- [ ] The same HTTP request returns the complete non-silent utterance, not just the initial 80 ms.
- [ ] Regression coverage exercises multiple audio chunks with a silent first chunk and verifies complete delivery/valid WAV framing.
- [ ] Frontend/worker compatibility is tested, rather than only replacing one side and assuming the protocol matches.
- [ ] Documentation uses `curl -o output.wav` for raw speech output and does not require a JSON envelope for this path.

## Validation boundary and cleanup

Only the stated stock-release failure and diagnostic comparisons have been verified. No patched end-to-end deployment is claimed. Temporary test DGDs were removed after capture; source/example code and shared controllers were not changed. Full local manifests, requests, redacted logs, runtime sources, media, hashes, and cleanup evidence were retained; private cluster diagnostics are intentionally not pasted into this public issue.
